body: Language models can score psychiatric questionnaires from speech, but agreement with self-report may reflect the questionnaire rather than the person. We introduce psychometric representational similarity analysis, a framework for comparing the structure of speech-derived scores, self-report, item wording and theory, and implement it alongside person-level construct scoring in COMPASS 2.0. We show how similarly worded items induce covariance without psychological signal. In pre-registered discovery and confirmation analyses of clinical interviews from 275 participants, language-derived symptom geometry resembled wording more than self-report, with no structure beyond wording detected by the registered tests. Geometric agreement with self-report survived assigning participants someone else's answers, whereas person-paired scores captured distress more than specific symptoms. Complementary analyses examined counselling quality and wording structure across 34 instruments and the Research Domain Criteria (RDoC) framework. These findings distinguish agreement about psychological structure from evidence that language-derived assessments track individual people.
summaryZh: 本文介绍了 COMPASS 2.0 框架，旨在通过心理测量学表征相似性分析来区分语言模型评估中的“症状结构”与“个人信号”。研究发现，模型对心理问卷的评分往往更多地反映了问卷本身的措辞结构，而非真实的个人心理状态。该研究为评估大模型在临床心理学应用中的有效性提供了新的分析视角。

aiReview.reasonZh: 该研究通过心理测量学分析揭示了语言模型在评估心理健康问卷时可能存在的偏差，对模型评估方法论有重要意义。
